title: How to design sheet metal parts for laser cutting
heading: How to design sheet metal parts for laser cutting, with AI and a DXF flat pattern
description: Design a bent sheet metal part with AI and get the flat pattern as a DXF for a laser cutting service, with bend lines and a bend table. Step by step in SOMA.
summary: A bent sheet metal motor bracket designed by AI around real STEP files, unfolded into a DXF for the laser with bend lines and a drawing with a bend table.

video.title: AI Designed My Sheet Metal Stepper Bracket, DXF for the Laser Included (No CAD Skills)

chapters.label: The real parts: STEP files of the motor and the extrusion
How it is made: the sheet metal skill
Design the bracket in plain words
Flat pattern: DXF with bend lines, drawing with bend table
Change it: a tab with Mark up, a thicker sheet

answer: To design a sheet metal part for laser cutting, you need the bent part and its flat pattern: the unfolded outline as a DXF file at 1:1, with the bend lines kept apart from the lines to cut. In SOMA you set your material, thickness and bend radius once, describe the part to the AI agent in plain words, and it builds the bent part and writes the DXF and a drawing with a bend table. Check the flat size and the bend details with your laser cutting service before you order, because bend allowances depend on their machines and material.
need: SOMA, free and open source, for Windows, macOS or Linux.

A sign-in for SOMA AI: a ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan, or an API key from Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI, Google Gemini, OpenRouter or OpenCode. SOMA is free, the AI runs on your plan or key. The cheapest way to start is an OpenCode Go subscription for about $10 a month.
Your material, sheet thickness and inner bend radius. Ask your laser cutting service which ones they offer; the video uses 2 mm steel with a 2 mm inner bend radius.
STEP files of the parts your sheet metal part has to fit, if you have them. The video uses a NEMA 17 stepper motor and a piece of 2020 V-slot extrusion from the FreeCAD Parts Library.
In the video the agent is Claude Code; SOMA AI, built into SOMA, works the same way.

steps.title: Import the parts it has to fit
text: Start a new model and click Import at the top. Add the STEP files of the parts your bracket has to hold. SOMA puts them into the model's inputs folder, where the agent can use them.
Click a STEP file in Files to look at it in the 3D view. In the video it is the real motor: flange, shaft and connector, ten parts in all. Back to model returns to your model.

image.alt: A NEMA 17 stepper motor from a STEP file in SOMA's 3D view, labeled The real motor, 10 parts, with the banner Viewing inputs/NEMA_17_with_connector.step

steps.title: Set up the sheet metal skill
text: Skills tell the agent how your parts are made. Open Skills in the sidebar. Under Manufacturing there is Sheet metal, and also Laser cutting and Plasma cutting.

Click Sheet metal, set it to Always for this model and enter your material, sheet thickness and inner bend radius. The video uses steel (DC01), 2 mm thick, with a 2 mm inner bend radius and a K-factor of 0.4.
The agent then follows the skill's rules: distances from holes to bends, bend reliefs, and the flat pattern with the right K-factor.

image.alt: The Sheet metal skill card set to Always, with material Steel (DC01), sheet thickness 2 mm, inner bend radius 2 mm and K-factor 0.4

steps.title: Describe the part in plain words
text: Say what the part has to do, which parts it holds, how it is fastened and what you want to change later. If you do not want to answer questions, ask the agent to choose sensible values and tell you what it chose.

The agent measures the motor and the extrusion in the STEP files, picks the screws and builds the bracket. In the video it is a C-shaped channel: the plate holds the motor with the pilot hole and slots on the 31 mm hole pattern for the belt tension, and two flanges wrap around the extrusion and make it stiff.
The structure tree lists the bracket and the screws, with the motor and the extrusion as references. Explode and Section above the 3D view show how it goes together and how the bends look.
steps.prompt: In inputs are a NEMA 17 stepper motor and a 100 mm piece of 2020 V-slot extrusion. Design a bracket from bent sheet metal that holds the motor at one end of the extrusion, with the shaft pointing sideways, so a GT2 belt can run along the extrusion. Make the motor holes slots, so I can tension the belt. Fix it to the extrusion with M5 screws and T-nuts, add the screws, and show the motor and the extrusion in place, the extrusion lying horizontally. I want to change the sheet thickness later. Don't ask me, choose sensible values and tell me what you chose.

image.alt: Close-up of the bent sheet metal bracket: the motor plate with slotted screw holes and the shaft, a bent flange over the V-slot extrusion with M5 screws

steps.title: Ask for the flat pattern as a DXF
text: A laser cuts a flat sheet, so the service needs the part unfolded: the flat pattern. It comes as a DXF file, a common 2D drawing format that laser cutting services accept.

Ask for the outline and holes to cut, and for the bend lines on their own layer, so they are marked but not cut. The agent unfolds the bracket; each bend adds a little length, worked out from the radius, the thickness and the K-factor.
Click the DXF in Files and SOMA opens it in its DXF view: the outline and holes to cut, and the bend lines on their own layer, which you can turn off and on.
steps.prompt: Now the flat pattern for the laser cutting service: a DXF file with the outline and the holes to cut, and the bend lines on their own layer. Update it every time the model is built. Show the flat blank next to the bracket too. And make a drawing of the flat pattern with a bend table.

image.alt: The DXF view in SOMA: the flat blank with the motor pilot hole, four slots and two holes, and two red bend lines across it

steps.title: Check the drawing with the bend table
text: Open Drawings in the sidebar. The drawing shows the flat blank with its size and a table with every bend: its direction, angle, inner radius, K-factor and bend allowance.
Send the drawing along with the DXF, so the service knows how to bend the part. Export at the top of Drawings saves the sheets as PDF or DXF.

image.alt: The drawing Motor bracket flat pattern: the dimensioned flat blank and a bend table with direction, angle, inner radius, K-factor and bend allowance for two bends

steps.title: Add a detail with Mark up
text: Click Mark up, draw the new feature where you want it, write what it is, then Send to agent and add one sentence. In the video a small tab for a limit switch appears with its own bend and holes for the switch, and the flat pattern grows with it.
steps.prompt: Add a small tab here for a limit switch, a standard micro switch with two M2 holes 9.5 mm apart, bent like the rest.

steps.title: Change the thickness and send the DXF
text: Because the prompt asked for it, the sheet thickness is in the Parameters tab. Change it, for example from 2 to 3 mm, and SOMA rebuilds the bracket. The flat pattern gets the new bend allowance, and the DXF is updated with it.
Open the DXF again to check it, then upload it to a laser cutting service, bend the flanges and bolt the motor on.

tips: Ask your laser cutting service for their materials, thicknesses and bend radii first, and enter those in the sheet metal skill. The flat pattern is only right for the values it was calculated with.
Ask for the bend lines on their own layer. Then the laser cuts only the outline and holes, and the bend lines still show where to bend.
Ask for the DXF to be updated on every build. Then a change in the Parameters tab or by the agent never leaves you with an old flat pattern.
If you cut your own parts on a plasma table, there is a Plasma cutting skill as well.
For the best results the user guide recommends Opus 5.5 (with an API key) or GPT-6 Astra (with ChatGPT), with High effort or more.

faq.q: What file does a laser cutting service need?
faq.a: Most laser cutting services want a 2D DXF file of the flat part at a scale of 1:1, in millimeters, with only the lines to cut. For a part that will be bent, that is the flat pattern, and the bend lines should be on their own layer or marked so they are not cut. They also need the material, the thickness and, for bending, the bend angles and radii.

faq.q: What is a flat pattern in sheet metal?
faq.a: The flat pattern is the bent part unfolded into the flat sheet it is cut from. It is slightly different from simply adding up the outside dimensions, because the metal stretches and compresses in each bend. The difference is the bend allowance, calculated from the bend radius, the thickness and the K-factor.

The K-factor tells where in the sheet's thickness the material neither stretches nor compresses when it is bent, as a fraction of the thickness. It is used to calculate how long the flat part must be. It depends on the material and the bending process, so use the value your bending service gives you; the video uses 0.4 for 2 mm steel.

faq.q: Can I design sheet metal parts without CAD skills?
faq.a: Yes. In SOMA you describe the part in plain words and its AI agent builds the bent part, the flat pattern as a DXF and a drawing with a bend table. You set the material, thickness and bend radius once, and change sizes later with sliders. Check the flat size and the bends with your service before ordering.

faq.q: What happens to the flat pattern when I change the sheet thickness?
faq.a: A different thickness changes the bend allowance, so the flat pattern changes too. In SOMA the agent can keep the DXF up to date on every build, so after you change the thickness in the Parameters tab, the flat pattern and the DXF follow.
